items.claim: The span Ezek.4.1-Ezek.4.17 is a coherent commanded-action complex and it holds, but the row rejects the 4:1-3 against 4:4-17 division without naming either piece of evidence that stands on that division's close side: a samekh is recorded after MT 4:3, and Ezek.4.3 ends on the sign colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ('it is a sign to the house of Israel'), the free-standing noun for 'sign' standing on 1 verse in the book (sweep: the free-standing token, 1 verse, Ezek.4.3). A samekh after MT 4:15 is likewise inside the span and unnamed, while the samekh marks after MT 4:12 and MT 4:14 are disclosed. The row also says the continuing commands open with a bare 'and you' at 4:4 and 4:9; Ezek.4.3 opens the same way (וְאַתָּ֤ה קַח לְךָ֙), so the span carries three such commands, not two.
items.both_sides: Seam 4:3/4:4 weighed from both sides. Close side: Ezek.4.3 ends on the sign colophon and a samekh stands after MT 4:3, which together make it the one interior point in the span with a genre label and a Masoretic break behind it. Onset side: Ezek.4.4 opens וְאַתָּ֤ה שְׁכַב֙, a bare 'and you' with an imperative beginning a different symbolic action, the bearing of the iniquity of the house of Israel by lying on the side; that construction is not among the devices the book's ruled granularity licenses for a row onset, so the mark has no formula opposite it and does not cut. The WEB paragraph standing at web:Ezek.4.4 is translation-layer texture and carries no boundary weight. The span therefore holds at 17 verses with its cap disclosure, and the close-side evidence belongs on the record because it is the whole of the case for the alternative the row names and rejects. refs_mirror flag on this row: the unmirrored refs are Ezek.3.25, Ezek.3.27 and Ezek.5.1, the adjacent units' anchor verses argued in prose; no literary-form defect in them.

items.claim: The span Ezek.5.1-Ezek.5.17 holds and closes correctly at 5:17, but Ezek.5.13 is weighed at the weaker of its two values on exactly the question the row is answering. Its close reads וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ ('and they shall know that I, Yahweh, have spoken'): the recognition refrain in its third-person form, which the device census lists among the 28 strict-form recognition verses, fused with the emphatic 'I Yahweh have spoken'. The row names 5:13 only as one of the three occurrences of the emphatic close, so the span's strongest interior close device is never identified as a refrain, in a row whose close argument turns on which of the three occurrences is unit-final.
items.both_sides: Seam 5:13/5:14 weighed from both sides. Close side: Ezek.5.13 carries two refrain-grade devices at once, the recognition refrain and the emphatic close, which is stronger than any other interior point in the span. Onset side: Ezek.5.14 opens וְאֶתְּנֵךְ֙ לְחָרְבָּ֣ה ('and I will make you a waste'), a continuation with no messenger formula, word-event or address restarting the speech, so nothing licenses an onset there and the unit cannot end at 5:13. The close therefore stays at 5:17, where the emphatic formula stands with a pe recorded after MT 5:17. A second alternative the row does not weigh: the 5:4/5:5 division between the commanded action and its interpretation, with a pe recorded after MT 5:4 on the close side and the messenger formula opening Ezek.5.5 on the onset side. It does not cut, because no refrain-grade close stands at 5:4 and the interpretation is bound to the action by the clause shared between Ezek.5.2 and Ezek.5.12 (sweep: 3 verses carry that clause, the third at Ezek.12.14); but at 17 verses the span is past the ruled stretch, and that is the alternative the weighing should address. refs_mirror flag on this row: the unmirrored refs are the whole of Ezek.4.1-Ezek.4.17 plus Ezek.6.1 and Ezek.12.14, produced by a verse range cited in prose and by two cross-unit anchors; no literary-form defect in them.

items.claim: The span Ezek.7.1-Ezek.7.4 holds with both edges marked, but Ezek.7.2 carries three frame devices at once and the row discloses none of them, citing 7:2 only for its ketiv/qere. Its opening reads וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם כֹּה אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה: the 'and you, son of man' construction (sweep: 23 verses book-wide carry it, Ezek.7.2 among them), which is the very construction the two adjacent commanded-action units take as their own onsets at Ezek.4.1 and Ezek.5.1; the 'son of man' address, an inventory member of the 93; and the messenger formula, an inventory member of the 122. The row's signal keys carry neither the messenger entry nor the address entry.
items.both_sides: Seam 7:1/7:2 is interior and not a cut candidate, weighed from both sides: Ezek.7.1 is a word-event onset in its strict form and Ezek.7.2 supplies that word-event's content, so the construction there opens the speech and not a unit. That is exactly the distinction the adjacent rows turn on, where the same construction does open a unit at Ezek.4.1 and Ezek.5.1 with no word-event in front of it. The row's own edges hold from both sides: onset, the word-event at Ezek.7.1 with the pe recorded after MT 6:14 behind it; close, the second-person-plural recognition refrain at Ezek.7.4 with a pe recorded after MT 7:4, and a fresh messenger formula at Ezek.7.5 in front. refs_mirror flag on this row: the unmirrored refs are Ezek.3.16, Ezek.6.1, Ezek.6.14 and the range Ezek.7.5-Ezek.7.27, produced by a recurrence comparison and by a verse range cited in the rejected alternative; no literary-form defect in them.

items.claim: The span Ezek.7.5-Ezek.7.9 holds, but its load-bearing sentence gives the shared eye-and-pity clause the wrong role. The clause at Ezek.7.9, וְלֹא תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמ֑וֹל, is shared with Ezek.7.4 and recurs across unit boundaries (sweep: 5 verses carry it, Ezek.5.11, Ezek.7.4, Ezek.7.9, Ezek.8.18 and Ezek.9.10), so a device straddling the 7:4/7:5 seam is continuity evidence against that seam, not close evidence for the seam at 7:9/7:10. The sharing is wider than the clause: Ezek.7.8-Ezek.7.9 repeats Ezek.7.3-Ezek.7.4 across the seam almost word for word, Ezek.7.3 and Ezek.7.8 both ending וּשְׁפַטְתִּ֖יךְ כִּדְרָכָ֑יִךְ וְנָתַתִּ֣י עָלַ֔יִךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל תּוֹעֲבֹתָֽיִךְ with Ezek.7.8 differing only in the plene spelling of the last word, and Ezek.7.4 and Ezek.7.9 sharing the eye-and-pity clause, the ways-and-abominations clause and the recognition refrain. The seam at 7:9/7:10 rests on the refrain at 7:9 and on the absence of any device at 7:10, which is sufficient without the shared clause.
items.both_sides: Seam 7:4/7:5 weighed from both sides: close side, the recognition refrain at Ezek.7.4 with a pe recorded after MT 7:4; onset side, the messenger formula opening Ezek.7.5. The seam stands, and the two-verse repetition across it is the continuity disclosure the corpus requires against it, since the two panels are a matched pair rather than two unrelated oracles. Seam 7:9/7:10 weighed from both sides: close side, the second-person-plural refrain at Ezek.7.9 with its appended participle and no mark after it, which the row correctly discloses as an absence; onset side, Ezek.7.10 opens הִנֵּ֥ה הַיּ֖וֹם הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֑ה and carries no frame device at all, so the cut rests on the close alone. That is thinner than a medium_low reading suggests, and the alternative is a single 23-verse span; the cut is defensible, but its ground is the refrain and the ruled granularity, not the shared clause. refs_mirror flag on this row: the unmirrored refs are Ezek.5.11, Ezek.8.18, Ezek.9.10 and the range Ezek.7.10-Ezek.7.27, produced by the sweep citation and by a verse range cited in the rejected alternative; no literary-form defect in them.

items.claim: The span Ezek.7.10-Ezek.7.27 holds and low confidence is the right level for it, but the pe recorded after MT 7:22 is weighed from its near side only. On the far side Ezek.7.23 opens עֲשֵׂ֖ה הָֽרַתּ֑וֹק ('make the chain'), a second-person imperative addressed to the prophet standing immediately after that mark, and the row names the mark as interior texture without naming what stands beyond it, in an eighteen-verse span past the ruled stretch whose own onset verse carries no frame device.

Close side: Ezek.7.22 ends וּבָאוּ בָ֥הּ פָּרִיצִ֖ים וְחִלְּלֽוּהָ, a narrative continuation with no refrain, so the pe recorded after MT 7:22 is the only close-side signal there. Onset side: Ezek.7.23 opens on an imperative to the prophet, a command form the book's ruled onset set does not license as a row onset, and the WEB paragraph at web:Ezek.7.23 is translation-layer texture with no boundary weight. With a mark on one side and no licensed device on the other, the seam does not cut, and the span stands to the recognition refrain at Ezek.7.27 with a pe recorded after MT 7:27, the dateline at Ezek.8.1 being the next hard seam. The row's own onset at Ezek.7.10 carries no device, which the row discloses, and that is what holds the confidence down. refs_mirror flag on this row: the unmirrored refs are Ezek.7.5-Ezek.7.8, the preceding unit's verses argued in prose; no literary-form defect in them.
